opening: The record concerns an icebound research vessel changing watches during a storm. By the time investigators reconstructed the emergency ballast release, casual impressions had produced several plausible candidates. The reviewers therefore used only the local rules stated in the surviving record.

scenes.prose: Before comparing names, the panel read the governing notes aloud. For this incident, the board declared the concordant watchkeeper protocol active; ordinary rank and reputation did not count. The panel fixed one shared status scale for the whole inquiry: clear counted as 0; open counted as 1; dormant counted as 2; waking counted as 3; stable counted as 4; latent counted as 5. The local tally began at 17. In order it used relation, temporal, causal, spatial, sequence, and protocol statuses with coefficients 13, 11, 2, 3, 5, 7. At each stream, the panel squared the current tally, added that stream's coefficient times its status value, and kept the remainder modulo 97. It made three passes: first in the stated order, then in reverse order with the coefficients reversed, then once more in the stated order with the coefficient list rotated one place left. Without resetting the tally, it repeated that complete three-pass cycle 126 times.
scenes.title: Reconstruction 1

scenes.prose: The inquiry moved from recollection to checked records. When the pairing sheet was recovered, Tatum Silva's mentor pennant stood at dormant. Even the damaged roster still marked Eden Okada's mentor pennant as stable. A clock-backed entry listed Tatum Okada's watch interval as stable. The alarm consequence that followed Morgan Kline registered as waking. Causal review marked Morgan Andersen's alarm consequence dormant. Door and route checks placed Tatum Silva's assigned station at stable. Witnesses in the corridor put Eden Okada's assigned station at latent. Reconstruction kept Tatum Okada's handover order at dormant. A close photograph of the token set Morgan Kline's seal notch to clear. At final count, Morgan Andersen's seal notch remained open.
scenes.title: Reconstruction 2

scenes.prose: The inquiry moved from recollection to checked records. A witness who checked the roster left Morgan Kline with a latent mentor pennant. On the sealed worksheet, clerks wrote clear beside Morgan Andersen's mentor pennant. Clocked entries put Tatum Silva's watch interval at waking. The sequence sheet showed Eden Okada's watch interval as latent. Downstream checks tied Tatum Okada to a latent alarm consequence. A movement sketch marked Morgan Kline's assigned station as clear. The route ledger tied Morgan Andersen's assigned station to open. In the ordered log, Tatum Silva's handover order appeared as clear. The ordered sheet showed Eden Okada's handover order as open. Inventory counted Tatum Okada's seal notch as stable.
scenes.title: Reconstruction 3

scenes.prose: The inquiry moved from recollection to checked records. In the earlier pairing note, Tatum Okada carried a open mentor pennant. After the timesheet review, Morgan Kline's watch interval stayed clear. Reconciled timing notes kept Morgan Andersen's watch interval at dormant. Instruments tracing Tatum Silva's action left the alarm consequence clear. When Eden Okada acted, the alarm consequence came back stable. Location review left Tatum Okada's assigned station waking. Sequence notes placed Morgan Kline's handover order at latent. At sequence review, Morgan Andersen's handover order stayed stable. Token and seal checks left Tatum Silva's seal notch at waking. The sealed check showed Eden Okada's seal notch as dormant.
scenes.title: Reconstruction 4

scenes.prose: The inquiry moved from recollection to checked records. For this incident, the accepted tally was 4. The final definition was strict: the concordant watchkeeper was the one person whose six-stream tally equaled the accepted tally.
